label: Robbery
statementOfOffence: Robbery, contrary to section 8(1) of the Theft Act 1968.

precedents.name: R v Hale
precedents.principle: Robbery may be a continuing act; force used during escape can suffice.

precedents.name: R v Dawson and James
precedents.principle: Even minimal force may be sufficient for robbery.

precedents.name: R v Robinson
precedents.principle: Force must be used in order to steal.

precedents.name: R v Jogee
precedents.principle: Clarifies approach to joint enterprise liability.

templates.particularsStarter: On [date] at [place], the defendant robbed [victim] of [property], using [force or threats].

label: Possession of a controlled drug (Class A)
statementOfOffence: Possession of a controlled drug of Class A, contrary to section 5(2) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.

precedents.name: R v Warner
precedents.principle: Knowledge of the existence of the substance is required.

precedents.name: R v Boyesen
precedents.principle: Possession requires custody or control together with knowledge.

precedents.name: R v Lambert
precedents.principle: Reverse burden issues regarding lack of knowledge.

templates.particularsStarter: On [date] at [place], the defendant had in their possession [drug].

precedents.name: R v Warner
precedents.principle: Knowledge of the existence of the substance is required.

precedents.name: R v Boyesen
precedents.principle: Possession requires custody or control together with knowledge.

label: Assault by beating (common assault)

statementOfOffence: Assault by beating, contrary to section 39 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988.

label: Assault occasioning actual bodily harm (ABH)
policeCharge: ASSAULT OCCASIONING ACTUAL BODILY HARM, contrary to section 47 of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861. On the 18th day of November 2025, at 1 High Street, Manchester, VICTOR DANVERS assaulted Andrew Thomas, thereby occasioning them actual bodily harm.
statementOfOffence: Assault occasioning actual bodily harm, contrary to section 47 of the Offences Against the Person Act 1861.

label: Fraud by false representation
policeCharge: FRAUD BY FALSE REPRESENTATION, contrary to section 2 of the Fraud Act 2006. On the 18th day of November 2025, at 1 High Street, Manchester, VICTOR DANVERS dishonestly made a false representation to Eddie Danvers, namely offering fake football finals tickets for money, intending to make a gain for himself or to cause loss to another.
statementOfOffence: Fraud by false representation, contrary to section 2 of the Fraud Act 2006.

precedents.name: R v Augunas
precedents.principle: A representation may be false even if it is literally true but misleading.

precedents.name: R v Barnard
precedents.principle: A false representation can be made by conduct.

templates.particularsStarter: On [date] at [place], the [defendant] dishonestly made a false representation, intending to make a gain for themselves or another, or to cause loss to another.

label: Threatening behaviour
policeCharge: THREATENING BEHAVIOUR, contrary to section 4 of the Public Order Act 1986. On the 18th day of November 2025, at 1 High Street, Manchester, LUCAS STARK used threatening behaviour towards Eddie Danvers, thereby causing him to fear that unlawful violence would be used against him.
statementOfOffence: Threatening behaviour, contrary to section 4 of the Public Order Act 1986.

precedents.name: R v Horseferry Road Magistrates' Court, ex p Siadatan
precedents.principle: Threatening words alone may suffice if intent to cause fear is present.

templates.particularsStarter: On [date] at [place], the defendant used threatening behaviour with intent to cause [victim] to fear immediate unlawful violence.
